chunks: And from him, from his father, from Hamza ibn Abdullah, from Jameel ibn Darraj, from Abu al-Walid, from Abu Baseer who said:
Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) said to me: 'O Abu Muhammad! Whenever you go to your wife, so which thing are you saying?'
I said, 'May I be sacrificed for you, and can I endure saying anything?'
He (peace be upon him) said: 'Yes. Say, O Allah! With Your Words do I permit her private parts, and by Your Security I take her.'
So if You were to Judge anything for me in her womb, so Make it to be pious, pure, and do not Make a participation for the Satan to be in it.'
He (Abu Baseer) said, 'I said, 'May I be sacrificed for you! And there happens to be a participation for the Satan therein?'
He (peace be upon him) said: 'Yes. Have you not heard the Words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, in His Book: and share with them in wealth and the children.'
The Satan comes over, so he sits just as the man sits (upon the wife) and descends just as the man descends'.
I said, 'And by which thing is that recognised?'
He (peace be upon him) said: 'By love for us and hatred for us'.
ai.seo_question: What is the supplication to recite when approaching one's wife to ensure the child is free from the Satan's influence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi outlines the specific supplication for marital intimacy, emphasizing the spiritual safeguarding of offspring from Satan's influence by invoking Allah's covenant. It uniquely identifies the mark of Satan's 'share' in children as their affinity for or aversion to the Ahl al-Bayt, a concept rooted in Shia theology regarding divine love and enmity. The narration connects this personal spiritual practice to the broader Quranic theme of Satan's seduction in worldly matters, including wealth and progeny.
